verdict: GBP activity is the standout story this period, driving 42 total actions (23 directions, 17 web clicks, 2 calls) over 28 days, though GBP engagement dropped 87.5% in the last 7 days versus the prior 7, likely due to reduced profile visibility or seasonal demand. performance.verdict: No paid activity; organic GBP collapse is the real risk now.

findings.text: Zero paid spend across all 28 days — Meta and Google both dark. No CPL exists because no paid leads have been generated at all.
GBP actions collapsed to near-zero: last 3 days (Aug 30–Sep 1) sum to 0 actions vs prior 3 days (Aug 27–29) totalling 2, themselves down from a peak of 11 on Aug 25.
GA4 sessions spiked to 26 on Sep 1 — largest single day in the 45-day window — while GBP actions remained 0. Source of that traffic is unconfirmed.
28-day GHL pipeline shows null — 42 GBP actions over the period produced 0 recorded opportunities, suggesting intake is not capturing organic interest.

suggestions.text: Monitor GBP actions daily for 3 more days; if zero persists through Sep 5, escalate profile audit.
suggestions.monday_update: GBP actions have been 0 for the last 3 days (Aug 30–Sep 1), down from a 45-day high of 11 on Aug 25 and a 7d drop of -87.5%. No paid channels are active, making GBP the sole demand signal. If actions remain at 0 through Sep 5, escalate to a GBP profile audit (photo refresh, Q&A, post cadence) to rule out a visibility penalty before considering paid reactivation.

suggestions.text: Audit GHL intake flow: 42 GBP actions over 28 days produced 0 pipeline opportunities — likely a form or routing gap.
suggestions.monday_update: Over the last 28 days, 42 GBP actions (23 directions, 17 web clicks, 2 calls) have been recorded but GHL shows 0 opportunities created. This is an intake leak, not an ads problem. Verify that the GBP web-click destination captures contact info and routes to GHL, and that call tracking is connected. Success check: at least 1 GHL opportunity logged from organic traffic by Sep 9.

suggestions.text: Investigate Sep 1 GA4 spike of 26 sessions — confirm source before attributing to any channel or action.
